notes.type_correctness: All function signatures match existing codebase style. PauseModal.onSelect typed as (index: number) => void, consistent with HUD patterns. No implicit any introduced.
notes.pattern_adherence: 3-option OPTION_LABELS const array follows the same as const tuple pattern used elsewhere. restartGame() and navigateToTitle() follow the same teardown order (blur, modal, key listener) as resumeFromPause(). OPTION_COUNT = 3 constant in attachPauseKeyListener matches the array length correctly.
notes.test_coverage: 27 tests cover construction, show/hide, selection state, onSelect callback, three-option rendering, selection wrapping, resize, and visual prefix state. All acceptance criteria exercised. main.ts routing for Restart/Return to Title is not unit-tested (no main.ts test file) but is covered by code review — acceptable for wiring code.
notes.security: Pure UI state machine. No network I/O, no user data stored, no eval or dynamic code paths. window.location.reload() in navigateToTitle() fallback is a safe no-op guard path.
notes.architectural_alignment: PauseModal remains a dumb display component with no game-state knowledge. Routing to restartGame/navigateToTitle is correctly kept in main.ts. The createGameState() intro-phase guard in navigateToTitle() is defensive programming — functionally sound but slightly fragile if engine default phase changes; acceptable given the guard falls back to reload().
